stories.title: China mandates sustainability reporting for major firms
stories.summary: China has implemented sustainability reporting guidelines for constituent companies of major indices and dual-listed firms. Affected entities must prepare and disclose reports covering the 2025 calendar year by 30 April 2026. The guidelines took effect in May 2024, standardising disclosure requirements for large domestic and international market participants.

stories.title: FRC plans phased sustainability reporting for Bangladesh firms
stories.summary: The Financial Reporting Council is developing a roadmap to mandate sustainability reporting for local companies over the next seven years. Initially targeting the top 50 listed firms by revenue, the rules aim to align sustainability performance with financial disclosures. Regulatory compliance for some sectors begins in January 2028.

stories.title: Lupin ranked on global sustainability list
stories.summary: Lupin Limited secured the 318th position on the World's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 list by TIME and Statista. Selected from over 5,000 organizations, the firm was evaluated on 20 sustainability indicators. The company also holds a CDP A rating for climate change and water security efforts.

stories.title: 65 business and public sector representatives identify practical solutions for integrating ESG principles into companies
UN launches public register for corporate climate targets
stories.summary: Eighty signatories have joined a new United Nations reporting tool at COP31, allowing businesses and governments to publish climate transition trajectories. While the platform aims to increase transparency, market observers remain sceptical of voluntary mechanisms, noting persistent blind spots in corporate emissions accounting and uneven adoption across different regions.

stories.title: NRBC Bank releases second sustainability report
stories.summary: NRBC Bank has published its 2025 sustainability report, detailing progress in digital banking and rural financial inclusion. The document includes the bank's first assessment of financed emissions, which were estimated at 74,818 tonnes under the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials framework. The report follows Global Reporting Initiative standards.

stories.title: Arriva Group appoints new head of ESG
stories.summary: Robert Macdiarmid has joined Arriva Group as head of ESG, transitioning from his previous role at ZIGUP. With 25 years of experience in transport and real estate, Macdiarmid will oversee organisational governance and carbon reduction strategies. He previously served as head of sustainability in the UK Cabinet Office.

stories.title: Regulatory Review: Electrification target divisions, California emissions disclosures and EU climate progress - Sustaina
COP31 Opens With Calls To Honor Climate Finance Pledges - Eurasia Review
India carbon market seeks liquidity
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has recognised India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. While this provides a potential advantage for Indian exporters, the scheme currently lacks the liquidity and depth required to produce credible price signals. The market awaits further development to ensure effective carbon pricing.

stories.title: Egypt calls for tripling climate adaptation finance by 2035 at COP31 - Economy - Business - Ahram Online
Climate groups caution against carbon market deregulation
stories.summary: Human rights and climate organisations have warned against attempts to weaken rules for the Paris Agreement’s carbon-crediting mechanism at COP31. Some nations are pushing to relax requirements, arguing current standards are too stringent. Critics contend that deregulation threatens the credibility of global climate action and environmental integrity.

stories.title: Singapore authorizes Rwanda water filter carbon project
stories.summary: Singapore has authorized its first carbon credit project under a new framework, involving a water filter distribution scheme in Rwanda. Developed by Climate Bridge International, the project aims to provide safe water to 1.8 million people, reducing the need for firewood and lowering indoor air pollution and emissions.

stories.title: Dhaka seeks predictable climate finance at COP31, signs carbon market MoU with Singapore - www.daily-sun.com
Bangladesh and Singapore sign carbon market MoU
stories.summary: Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding at COP31 to cooperate on international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The agreement aims to facilitate climate finance and promote joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions between the two nations.

stories.title: Ghana secures 6.57 million forest carbon credits, expects US$43m in initial payments - Asaase Radio
Ghana issues forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has received 6.57 million carbon credits for forest protection efforts, becoming the first African country to participate in the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions program. The issuance covers 2.5 million hectares and marks the first time such credits have received the Core Carbon Principles label.

stories.title: COP31 climate finance falls $840 billion short
stories.summary: Brazil projects an $840 billion shortfall against the $1.3 trillion annual climate finance goal agreed upon at COP31. While island nations press for faster recovery cash, Western governments are currently prioritizing domestic living costs and security. The funding gap remains a significant feature of the ongoing summit.

stories.title: AIIB, Brazil deepen climate finance and carbon market cooperation at COP31 - Traders Union
UN insurers release resilience white paper at COP31
stories.summary: The UN Environment Programme’s Principles for Sustainable Insurance Initiative released a white paper at COP31. It outlines how the insurance industry can catalyze economic resilience against physical climate risks like wildfires and heatwaves. The paper arrives as the industry faces a widening gap in global insurance coverage.

stories.title: Lula re-election offers breathing space for COP31
stories.summary: The COP31 climate talks have gained political breathing space following Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election in Brazil. His victory is viewed as a significant win for the Amazon compared to the environmental deregulation proposed by his opponent. US midterm results have also loosened Donald Trump’s influence.

stories.title: Minister Simon Watts represents New Zealand at COP31 - Times.co.nz
Strongest El Niño in 1,000 years adds urgency to COP31
stories.summary: COP31 delegates are facing the strongest El Niño event in at least 1,000 years. The phenomenon has fueled global wildfires, crop failures, and flooding, adding pressure to summit negotiations regarding climate funding for vulnerable nations. The climate pattern is being described as a major risk multiplier.

stories.title: COP31 president calls for concrete climate targets
stories.summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum has urged states to stop delaying climate targets, stating that societies and young people expect concrete decisions. Kurum noted that while national capabilities vary, countries taking immediate measures gain a competitive advantage. The presidency is pushing for determination in countering climate change consequences.

stories.title: Ministers face pressure as COP31 hits week two
stories.summary: COP31 enters its second week with key political disagreements over emissions and finance still unresolved. Ministers are now under pressure to bridge negotiating deadlocks and turn political mandates into a final agreement. The first week has left significant business unfinished for the arriving delegates.

stories.title: Greece urges faster emissions cuts at COP31
stories.summary: Greek Environment Minister Stavros Papastavrou has called for faster greenhouse gas emissions cuts and stronger international cooperation. Reaffirming commitment to the 1.5 degrees Celsius goal, he stated that countries outside the European Union must also increase their efforts to reduce emissions during the summit.

stories.title: Finland publishes fossil fuel exit plan
stories.summary: Finland has released a fossil fuel exit plan as the first week of COP31 concludes without formal mention of the industry. Despite warnings that the world is on course to overshoot the 1.5℃ threshold, leaders have largely avoided the topic. The summit is currently at a tipping point.

stories.title: UN chief delivers farewell address at COP31
stories.summary: Outgoing UN Secretary General António Guterres used his final climate press conference to warn that peace cannot be built on a burning planet. He argued that poverty cannot be eradicated while climate disasters persist, urging that climate action remain central to all future global governance.

stories.title: Guterres urges successor to prioritize climate action
stories.summary: In his final address to the UN climate summit, outgoing Secretary General António Guterres insisted that climate action must remain central to the organization's work. He argued that his successor must maintain vocal support for environmental initiatives as a core component of the UN mandate.

stories.title: COP31 negotiators look to methane for quick win
stories.summary: Climate diplomats at COP31 are targeting methane as a potential quick fix to slow global warming. While carbon dioxide remains the primary driver of climate change, methane is more potent at trapping heat. Negotiators are hoping to secure a win on the super pollutant before the summit ends.

stories.title: Greta Thunberg criticizes government inaction at COP31
stories.summary: Greta Thunberg addressed the COP31 summit, stating that the planet is being killed by the same people who claim to be its rescuers. In her first appearance at the UN talks in five years, she excoriated world governments for their ongoing failure to prevent environmental breakdown.

stories.title: Nepali activists call for climate justice at COP31
stories.summary: Climate activists from Nepal held an event at COP31 to highlight the impact of disasters on communities that contribute the least to climate change. Following devastating mudslides in August, the group appealed for greater cross-border cooperation to address the recurring climate-related threats facing their region.

stories.title: Sink-float separation tanks market expands
stories.summary: The global sink-float separation tanks market is entering a phase of sustained expansion. Industries are increasingly using the technology to recover value from complex material streams, including construction waste and plastic recycling. The market is seeing more disciplined procurement behavior and a more diversified supply architecture.

stories.title: COP31: Circular economy must prioritise youth and workers, speakers warn - The Climate Watch
Jordan to pitch green ventures at investment forum
stories.summary: Jordan will present seven circular economy and agri-tech ventures at the upcoming Jordan-EU Investment Conference. The projects are designed to transform industrial and electronic waste into commercial products. The event will be held under the patronage of King Abdullah II with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

stories.title: Bisleri director discusses plastic waste management
stories.summary: Bisleri director K Ganesh says plastic remains integral to modern manufacturing, though managing its environmental footprint is a complex challenge for India. He notes that industry must look beyond regulatory compliance to examine business responsibility and the systems supporting sustainable resource use. The waste gap remains open.

stories.title: Czech firm turns plastic waste into hybrid pallets
stories.summary: Flexipal is producing hybrid pallets by combining wood with low-grade plastic waste, moving beyond simple plastic block manufacturing. The company is working with Brno University of Technology to develop robotic repair systems and circular designs. Waste that once headed to landfills is now being repurposed.

stories.title: UAE expands resource recovery projects
stories.summary: The UAE is scaling up recycling initiatives to convert waste into valuable resources, including biofuel production from used cooking oil and organic waste processing. ENOC Group and Dubai Municipality have partnered to collect oil from households and businesses for biodiesel conversion. Landfills are being bypassed for value.

stories.title: DLA Disposition Services: Critical Materials and Rare Earth Elements Resource Recovery Circular Economy - Defense Logist
Mintoo for mainstreaming waste management into climate action - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
India's EPR framework shifts plastic costs to businesses
stories.summary: India's Extended Producer Responsibility framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to manage plastic packaging after sale. The rules aim to shift costs from municipalities to businesses while mandating collection and recycling targets. A digital portal now tracks these obligations across four distinct packaging categories.

stories.title: Roswall confirms single point EPR reporting
stories.summary: Environmental official Roswall has confirmed that EPR reporting will move to a single point system under the Circular Economy Act. The change is intended to clarify how directives are interpreted, though the system currently remains behind a subscription wall for those seeking full access to the details.

stories.title: Algeria reviews circular economy progress at COP31
stories.summary: Minister Kaoutar Krikou told COP31 attendees that Algeria is encouraging youth and startups to engage in circular economy activities. The government claims involvement from more than 6,000 economic operators in environmental initiatives. The minister highlighted these efforts during a roundtable on zero waste and methane reduction.

stories.title: Vietnam drafts law to boost recycling industry
stories.summary: A draft law in Vietnam aims to treat recycled materials as goods and set mandatory recycling roadmaps to encourage long-term investment. The proposal seeks to improve financial mechanisms and ensure fair competition for businesses. Policy clarity is being positioned as the primary requirement for a recycling breakthrough.

stories.title: Eternal reassesses 2030 EV delivery target
stories.summary: Zomato and Blinkit parent Eternal is reconsidering its goal for a 100 percent electric delivery fleet by 2030. Chief Sustainability Officer Anjalli Ravi Kumar cited rapid business expansion and the evolving EV ecosystem as reasons for the delay. The company remains committed to the transition, eventually.

stories.title: COP31 recognises sustainable building designs
stories.summary: Nine buildings were honoured at COP31 for sustainable design and energy performance. The projects utilized passive cooling and climate-responsive construction to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The awards were co-convened by the UNEP-hosted Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction and the COP31 Türkiye presidency.

stories.title: India faces $8 trillion net zero power challenge
stories.summary: India's electricity demand could rise tenfold by 2070, requiring $8 trillion in investment for generation, storage and grid infrastructure. While renewables could provide 80 percent of power, the transition relies on grid flexibility. Gigawatts are currently the primary metric for tracking this shift toward cleaner energy.

stories.title: General Motors leads sustainability executive rankings
stories.summary: Sustainability Magazine has ranked General Motors executive Cassandra Garber as the top sustainability leader in the automotive industry. The list evaluates executives based on their influence over fleet CO2 rules and battery due diligence. These leaders have collectively spent over 125 years at their respective companies.

stories.title: Shell Egypt starts gas production at Mina West
stories.summary: Shell Egypt has begun gas production at the Mina West field three years after discovery. The project was developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and partners. It is intended to add a new source of domestic supply to the country's energy foundation.

stories.title: Microsoft May Abandon its Clean Energy Powered Data Centre Targets - EnergyNow.com
Southwire Recognized Among America's Greenest Companies for 2027 - StreetInsider
BASF secures renewable power for chemical production
stories.summary: BASF plans to power its European polyisobutene production entirely with renewable electricity starting in January 2027. The company will use long-term power purchase agreements and existing investments to meet the goal. Manufacturers across several industries are increasingly looking to reduce the carbon footprint of their value chains.

stories.title: Fourth Partner Energy signs renewable deal in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Fourth Partner Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding for a 2,000 crore investment in Andhra Pradesh. The company plans to develop two solar projects and a hybrid wind-solar facility. The investment is intended to expand the firm's existing portfolio of projects serving commercial and industrial customers.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh secures renewable energy investment pledges
stories.summary: Seventeen memoranda of understanding and three government orders signed at the CII Partnership Summit represent renewable energy investments worth 43,871 crore rupees. The state expects these projects to create employment for 4,700 people. The government has yet to provide a timeline for the actual deployment of funds.

stories.title: Renewable energy expansion reduces India fuel import costs
stories.summary: India avoided 9.4 lakh crore rupees in coal and natural gas import costs between 2011 and 2025 through renewable energy expansion, according to the International Energy Agency. Cumulative savings are estimated to reach 22.6 lakh crore rupees by 2030. The math assumes the trend continues as projected.

stories.title: IEA declares the arrival of the age of electricity
stories.summary: Fatih Birol of the International Energy Agency says the world has moved beyond the age of coal, oil and gas. Global electricity generation capacity is expected to double over the next decade as nations seek protection from fossil fuel price volatility. The transition is currently picking up speed.

research.title: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event
research.summary: NASA scientists warn that the rapidly intensifying 2026 El Niño could surpass the historic 1997-98 event, which triggered devastating weather extremes around the world. Satellite data reveal striking similarities between the two, raising the possibility of major rainfall and flooding this winter, although the exact impacts remain uncertain.

research.summary: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star. NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
